windows.name: read_file
windows.description: Read a file's content. Returns content, line count, size, and hash10 (short fingerprint) (for edit_file conflict detection). Pass "paths" (array) to read multiple files in one call — avoids N round-trips for N files.

path.description: File path (relative to workspace or absolute). Use this for a single file.

paths.description: Array of file paths to read in one call. Use this to batch-read multiple files efficiently.

start_line.description: Starting line number (1-indexed). Use this to read a specific section of a large file. When set, returns at most max_lines lines starting from this line. Default: 1.

max_lines.description: Max lines to read. Default is 2000. When start_line is used, this limits how many lines are returned.

max_line_chars.description: Max characters per line. Default is 1600. Prevents token explosion from single very long lines (minified JS/CSS, long JSON/base64, etc.). Lines longer than this are truncated with a marker so the AI knows content is incomplete.

windows.name: write_file
windows.description: Write content to a file (full overwrite). Creates parent directories if they do not exist. ⚠️ Use edit_file for partial modifications instead of reading and re-writing entire files. Returns the hash10 (short fingerprint) of the written content (normalized to LF), which can be used as expected_hash for subsequent edit_file calls.

path.description: File path (relative to workspace or absolute).

windows.name: edit_file
windows.description: Replace exact text in a file. Requires expected_hash10 from read_file (conflict detection). Prefer for partial edits over write_file. Use the "edits" array to apply one or more edits in a single call — each edit is { old_string, new_string, replace_count }.

path.description: File path (relative to workspace or absolute).

edits.description: Array of edits to apply sequentially in one file. Each item: { old_string, new_string, replace_count }. All edits share the same expected_hash10 and are applied in order on the same content. Use this instead of multiple edit_file calls to avoid hash conflicts between edits.

old_string.description: The exact existing text to replace. Include enough surrounding context for a unique match.

new_string.description: The new text to insert in place of old_string.

replace_count.description: How many occurrences of old_string to replace. Default: 1. Set to 0 to replace all.

expected_hash.description: The hash10 value of the current file content, obtained from read_file output. Used for conflict detection to ensure no one modified the file since you read it.

windows.name: delete_file
windows.description: Delete one or more files/directories. Accepts either "path" (single string) or "paths" (array of strings). Deleted items are moved to trash/recycle bin.

path.description: Path to the file or directory to delete. Use this for a single item. (Deprecated in favor of "paths".)

paths.description: Array of paths to delete. Use this to delete multiple files/directories in one call.

items.description: Path to the file or directory to delete.

windows.name: copy_move_file
windows.description: Copy or move a file or directory. By default moves (renames) the source to destination. Set mode="copy" to copy instead. Note: copy mode only supports files, not directories; use move mode for directories.

source.description: Source file or directory path (relative to workspace or absolute).

destination.description: Destination file or directory path (relative to workspace or absolute).

mode.description: Operation mode: "move" (default) to move/rename, "copy" to copy.

windows.name: list_files
windows.description: List files and directories in a given path. Shows relative paths from the given root.

path.description: Directory path. Default: workspace root.

recursive.description: Whether to list recursively. Default: false

windows.name: file_info
windows.description: Get metadata about a file or directory.

path.description: Path to the file or directory.

windows.name: mkdir
windows.description: Create a directory (or directories). Pass "paths" (array) to create multiple directories in one call. By default creates parent directories if they do not exist (recursive=true). If a directory already exists, it is treated as success (idempotent).

path.description: Directory path to create (relative to workspace or absolute). Use this for a single directory.

paths.description: Array of directory paths to create in one call. Use this to batch-create multiple directories.

recursive.description: Whether to create parent directories if they do not exist. Default: true.

windows.name: search_files_by_name
windows.description: Search for files by filename. Supports plain text (case-insensitive substring match), regex matching (use_regex=true), or glob patterns (glob=true, e.g. "**/*.ts", "*.json", "src/**/*.css"). Returns a list of matching file paths.

path.description: Root directory to search in (e.g. "./src").

query.description: Filename pattern. Plain text (case-insensitive) by default, regex if use_regex=true, glob pattern if glob=true (e.g. "**/*.ts", "*.json", "src/**/*.css").

use_regex.description: Whether query is a regex pattern. Default: false.

glob.description: Whether query is a glob pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "*.json"). When true, overrides use_regex — converts glob to regex automatically. Default: false.

windows.name: search_text_in_files
windows.description: Search for text content inside files recursively. **Supports regex patterns.** Returns file path, line number, and the matching line content. Automatically skips binary files and respects .gitignore. Use this to find function definitions, variable usages, error messages, TODO comments, etc.

path.description: Root directory to search in (e.g. "./src").

query.description: Text or regex pattern to search for in file contents. Supports full regex syntax (e.g. "function\s+\w+" for function definitions, "TODO|FIXME" for TODOs).

windows.name: execute_command
windows.description: Execute an arbitrary shell command. The current terminal is Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe), so use PowerShell syntax (not cmd). Use this tool only when no dedicated tool exists (git, npm, builds, etc.). Prefer the dedicated tools (read_file, edit_file, write_file, search_*, ...) for file/text operations. The first line of the result is a "terminal environment" notice reporting the sandbox mode — "write isolation" (writes are allowed only inside the workspace/whitelisted writable roots; writes outside are rejected), "read-only" (no writes), or "no sandbox" (full permissions). An exit code >= 2 means the command failed.

command.description: The shell command to execute (PowerShell syntax), e.g. "Get-ChildItem", "git status", "node --version". Supports pipelines, redirection (>$null / 2>$null) and sequential execution separated by semicolons; does not support && / ||.

tips.description: A brief explanation of what this command does and why it is being run (use the user's language). It is shown in the UI to help the user understand the purpose of the command.

sandbox.description: Omit by default (inherits the sandbox mode from settings). Passing "off" **requests** execution without the sandbox, and should only be used for cases that are bound to fail under the sandbox: the command's child process needs to spawn a grandchild process with piped stdio (vitest / vite / jest / ts-node / node-gyp / child_process.exec*, etc.), and the sandbox's restricted token makes that spawn fail immediately with EPERM (the log looks like "spawn EPERM"). This request goes through the "sandbox bypass" permission (a confirmation dialog by default; it can be set to allow or deny); in read-only sandbox mode it is rejected outright.

confirm.description: Passing "terminal" means "confirm in the terminal before executing": the command is shown as a single **editable** line, and actually runs only after the user edits it if needed and presses Enter; Esc cancels. Suited to commands the user must sign off on and may rewrite (e.g. commands that need login or input such as npm login / gh auth login). Execution still goes through the same sandbox path (a command written by the user is not exempt from checks); supported only on the Windows desktop, and falls back to the approval dialog when unavailable.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds. The process is killed after this period. Default: 30.

windows.name: execute_script
windows.description: Create a script file (file_path + file_content), then execute it with a shell command, and by default delete the script file right after execution (end_del_file=true). Use this instead of execute_command when the code to run is long/multi-line and awkward to inline. The file is written through the same sandbox check as write_file; the command goes through the same approval flow as execute_command. The first line of the result is a "terminal environment" notice; an exit code >= 2 means the command failed.

file_path.description: Path of the script file (relative to the workspace, or absolute), e.g. "temp/run.js". A sandbox check runs before writing.

file_content.description: Content of the script file (full overwrite). Missing parent directories are created automatically.

command.description: The command used to run the script file (PowerShell syntax), e.g. "node script.js", "python task.py", ".\run.ps1". Reference the script file given by file_path; supports pipelines, redirection and sequential execution separated by semicolons; does not support && / ||.

tips.description: A brief explanation of what this command does and why it is being run (use the user's language). It is shown in the UI to help the user understand the purpose of the command.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds. The process is killed after this period. Default: 30.

sandbox.description: Omit by default (inherits the sandbox mode from settings). Passing "off" **requests** execution of the script without the sandbox, and should only be used for cases that are bound to fail under the sandbox (e.g. a child process inside the script needs to spawn a grandchild process with piped stdio). This request is decided by the "sandbox bypass · script execution" permission (a confirmation dialog by default); in read-only sandbox mode it is rejected outright.

end_del_file.description: Whether to delete the script file immediately after execution (including on failure/timeout). Default: true. Set to false to keep the script for troubleshooting.

windows.name: search_knowledge_base
windows.description: Search the knowledge base for relevant information. Use this tool when you need to answer questions based on uploaded documents, private data, or any content stored in the knowledge base. Returns relevant text chunks with similarity scores and source document names. The results can be used as context to answer user questions accurately. Always call list_knowledge_bases first to discover available knowledge bases, then use the correct knowledge_base_id for your search.

query.description: The search query. Be specific and use keywords for better results.

knowledge_base_id.description: The ID of the knowledge base to search in. Use list_knowledge_bases tool to see available knowledge bases and their IDs.

top_k.description: Number of relevant chunks to return. Default: 5, Max: 20.

windows.name: list_knowledge_bases
windows.description: List all available knowledge bases. Returns the name, description, ID, and document count for each knowledge base. Use this tool to discover which knowledge bases are available before searching or writing. The ID field is required for search_knowledge_base and write_to_knowledge_base tools.

windows.name: list_knowledge_base_documents
windows.description: List all documents in a specific knowledge base. Returns the document name, ID, file type, chunk count, and status for each document. Use this tool to discover document IDs needed for delete_knowledge_base_document. Use list_knowledge_bases first to discover available knowledge base IDs.

knowledge_base_id.description: The ID of the knowledge base to list documents from. Use list_knowledge_bases tool to see available knowledge bases.

windows.name: get_knowledge_base_document
windows.description: Get the full content of a specific document in a knowledge base. Returns all text content of the document, which can be used for deep analysis, summarization, or extracting specific information. Use list_knowledge_base_documents first to find the document ID, then use this tool to retrieve the full content.

knowledge_base_id.description: The ID of the knowledge base containing the document. Use list_knowledge_bases tool to see available knowledge bases.

document_id.description: The ID of the document to retrieve. Use list_knowledge_base_documents to find document IDs.

windows.name: write_to_knowledge_base
windows.description: Write text content to a knowledge base. Use this tool to save useful information, summaries, extracted knowledge, or any content that should be stored for future reference and search. The content will be automatically chunked, embedded, and indexed for semantic search. Use list_knowledge_bases first to discover available knowledge bases and their IDs.

knowledge_base_id.description: The ID of the knowledge base to write to. Use list_knowledge_bases tool to see available knowledge bases and their IDs.

document_name.description: A descriptive name for this document (e.g., "Meeting Notes - Q4 Planning", "Research Summary - Rust vs Go"). This helps users identify the content later.

content.description: The text content to save. This can include formatted text, code snippets, structured data, etc. The content will be automatically indexed and made searchable.

windows.name: delete_knowledge_base_document
windows.description: Delete a document from a knowledge base. Use this tool to remove outdated or incorrect documents from a knowledge base. The document and all its chunks will be permanently removed and will no longer be searchable. Use list_knowledge_bases to discover knowledge base IDs, then use list_knowledge_base_documents to find document IDs within a knowledge base.

knowledge_base_id.description: The ID of the knowledge base containing the document. Use list_knowledge_bases tool to see available knowledge bases.

document_id.description: The ID of the document to delete. Use list_knowledge_base_documents to find document IDs within a knowledge base.

windows.name: web_search
windows.description: Search the internet for up-to-date information. Use this tool when you need current data, recent news, or information not available in your training data. The search is powered by a configurable search provider (e.g., Tavily, Bing, SearXNG). Returns search results with titles, URLs, and snippets. When include_content=true, also returns the full page content when the provider supports it.

query.description: The search query. Be specific and use keywords for better results.

max_results.description: Maximum number of search results to return. Default: 10, Max: 50.

time_range.description: Time range filter for the search results. "day" = past 24h, "week" = past week, "month" = past month, "year" = past year. Use this when the user asks for recent or latest information.

windows.name: web_fetch
windows.description: Fetch a URL. Returns Markdown (if htmlToMd=true).

windows.name: vision_analyze
windows.description:
Run a complete visual analysis of an image; a single call returns all detection results:
[UI element detection] Detects buttons, icons, images, text blocks, containers, etc.
[OCR] Recognizes all text in the image.
[Icon recognition] Recognizes the meaning of 81 common icons.
[Object detection] Detects 254 everyday object classes (people, cars, phones, food, animals, etc.), with parent-child containment relations.
Output is tree text; coordinates use the [x,y w×h] format.
Suited to analysing UI screenshots, natural photos, and the like.

path.description: Absolute or relative path of the image file.

windows.name: list_skills
windows.description: List all skills the current agent has. Returns the skill names and descriptions so you know which skills you can use.

windows.name: read_skill_source
windows.description: Show the source-code directory structure of a given skill and the full text of its SKILL.md, and also return the skill folder's absolute path. Input the skill name (folder name); returns the list of all files in that skill directory, the full SKILL.md text, and the skill path. Once you have the skill path, you can use read_file to read other files under it.

name.description: Skill name (folder name), e.g. "code-reviewer". Use list_skills to see the names of all available skills.

windows.name: get_current_time
windows.description: Get the current date and time.

windows.name: user_choice
windows.description: Present a choice to the user. The AI provides a question, a list of options, and whether single or multiple selection is allowed. A dialog will pop up for the user to answer. The result is returned after the user confirms.

question.description: The question to ask the user

options.description: List of options for the user to choose from

multi.description: Whether multiple selection is allowed. If false, single selection.

windows.name: todo_write
windows.description: Create and update the task list (todos) for the current session. Always pass the COMPLETE list — this call REPLACES the previous list; an empty array clears it. Up to 50 items. Use it to plan multi-step work and keep progress visible: mark an item "in_progress" before starting it and "completed" IMMEDIATELY after finishing it. Keep at most ONE item "in_progress" at a time; the remaining items stay "pending". Reuse the same "id" when updating an item so the user (and the UI) can track it. Do not use it for a single trivial step.

todos.description: The complete task list, in execution order. Pass the full list on every call.

id.description: Stable id for the item (e.g. "1"). Reuse it when updating so progress stays trackable.

content.description: Imperative form, e.g. "Add unit tests for todo_write".

status.description: Task status. Exactly one item should be "in_progress" at a time.

activeForm.description: Present-continuous form shown while the item is in_progress, e.g. "Adding unit tests".

note.description: Optional one-line result or blocker note.

windows.name: list_messages
windows.description: List the timeline of messages that have been COMPRESSED AWAY in this conversation, i.e. earlier messages that are no longer present in your current context because the conversation was summarized. Messages that are still in your context are NOT returned — do not use this tool to re-read what you already have.  Each entry gives: sequence number (#seq), message ID, role, timestamp, a short preview (<= 100 chars) and the names of any tools the message called. Deep-thinking (reasoning) content is never exposed.  Use it to: (1) discover the message ID of an earlier message and then read it with read_messages; (2) find earlier messages by keyword. The newest page of the queryable range is returned first; to page further back, call again with the returned cursor.

cursor.description: Page cursor: only return messages with sequence before this value. Omit it to get the newest page of the queryable range.

keyword.description: Optional keyword filter applied to the message plain text. Only messages in the queryable (compressed) range are searched.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages per page. Default: 30, Max: 50.

windows.name: read_messages
windows.description: Read the full text of earlier messages that have been COMPRESSED AWAY (they are no longer in your current context). Only messages before the compression summary can be read; anything still in your context is NOT returned.  Provide message_id (obtained from list_messages) and a relative window:   [-10, 0] = the anchor and the 10 messages before it;   [0, 10]  = the anchor and the 10 messages after it;   [-5, 5]  = 5 before and 5 after (default). If message_id (and seq) are omitted, the newest readable message is used as the anchor.  Limits: at most 21 messages per call, each message text <= 4000 chars, each tool-call detail <= 100 chars. Deep-thinking (reasoning) content is never returned. Do not call this repeatedly to dump the whole history.

message_id.description: Anchor message ID (from list_messages). Preferred over seq.

seq.description: Anchor message sequence number, used when message_id is not provided.

window.description: Relative window [start, end] around the anchor, with start <= 0 <= end. Examples: [-10,0] (10 before), [0,10] (10 after), [-5,5] (default).

knowledge_base_id.description: The ID of the knowledge base to list documents from. Use list_knowledge_bases tool to see available knowledge bases.

macos.name: get_knowledge_base_document
macos.description: Get the full content of a specific document in a knowledge base. Returns all text content of the document, which can be used for deep analysis, summarization, or extracting specific information. Use list_knowledge_base_documents first to find the document ID, then use this tool to retrieve the full content.

knowledge_base_id.description: The ID of the knowledge base containing the document. Use list_knowledge_bases tool to see available knowledge bases.

document_id.description: The ID of the document to retrieve. Use list_knowledge_base_documents to find document IDs.

macos.name: write_to_knowledge_base
macos.description: Write text content to a knowledge base. Use this tool to save useful information, summaries, extracted knowledge, or any content that should be stored for future reference and search. The content will be automatically chunked, embedded, and indexed for semantic search. Use list_knowledge_bases first to discover available knowledge bases and their IDs.

knowledge_base_id.description: The ID of the knowledge base to write to. Use list_knowledge_bases tool to see available knowledge bases and their IDs.

document_name.description: A descriptive name for this document (e.g., "Meeting Notes - Q4 Planning", "Research Summary - Rust vs Go"). This helps users identify the content later.

content.description: The text content to save. This can include formatted text, code snippets, structured data, etc. The content will be automatically indexed and made searchable.

macos.name: delete_knowledge_base_document
macos.description: Delete a document from a knowledge base. Use this tool to remove outdated or incorrect documents from a knowledge base. The document and all its chunks will be permanently removed and will no longer be searchable. Use list_knowledge_bases to discover knowledge base IDs, then use list_knowledge_base_documents to find document IDs within a knowledge base.

knowledge_base_id.description: The ID of the knowledge base containing the document. Use list_knowledge_bases tool to see available knowledge bases.

document_id.description: The ID of the document to delete. Use list_knowledge_base_documents to find document IDs within a knowledge base.

macos.name: web_search
macos.description: Search the internet for up-to-date information. Use this tool when you need current data, recent news, or information not available in your training data. The search is powered by a configurable search provider (e.g., Tavily, Bing, SearXNG). Returns search results with titles, URLs, and snippets. When include_content=true, also returns the full page content when the provider supports it.

query.description: The search query. Be specific and use keywords for better results.

max_results.description: Maximum number of search results to return. Default: 10, Max: 50.

time_range.description: Time range filter for the search results. "day" = past 24h, "week" = past week, "month" = past month, "year" = past year. Use this when the user asks for recent or latest information.

macos.name: web_fetch
macos.description: Fetch a URL. Returns Markdown (if htmlToMd=true).

macos.name: vision_analyze
macos.description:
Run a complete visual analysis of an image; a single call returns all detection results:
[UI element detection] Detects buttons, icons, images, text blocks, containers, etc.
[OCR] Recognizes all text in the image.
[Icon recognition] Recognizes the meaning of 81 common icons.
[Object detection] Detects 254 everyday object classes (people, cars, phones, food, animals, etc.), with parent-child containment relations.
Output is tree text; coordinates use the [x,y w×h] format.
Suited to analysing UI screenshots, natural photos, and the like.

path.description: Absolute or relative path of the image file.

name.description: Skill name (folder name), e.g. "code-reviewer". Use list_skills to see the names of all available skills.

macos.name: get_current_time

macos.name: user_choice
macos.description: Present a choice to the user. The AI provides a question, a list of options, and whether single or multiple selection is allowed. A dialog will pop up for the user to answer. The result is returned after the user confirms.

question.description: The question to ask the user

options.description: List of options for the user to choose from

multi.description: Whether multiple selection is allowed. If false, single selection.

macos.name: todo_write
macos.description: Create and update the task list (todos) for the current session. Always pass the COMPLETE list — this call REPLACES the previous list; an empty array clears it. Up to 50 items. Use it to plan multi-step work and keep progress visible: mark an item "in_progress" before starting it and "completed" IMMEDIATELY after finishing it. Keep at most ONE item "in_progress" at a time; the remaining items stay "pending". Reuse the same "id" when updating an item so the user (and the UI) can track it. Do not use it for a single trivial step.

todos.description: The complete task list, in execution order. Pass the full list on every call.

id.description: Stable id for the item (e.g. "1"). Reuse it when updating so progress stays trackable.

content.description: Imperative form, e.g. "Add unit tests for todo_write".

status.description: Task status. Exactly one item should be "in_progress" at a time.

activeForm.description: Present-continuous form shown while the item is in_progress, e.g. "Adding unit tests".

note.description: Optional one-line result or blocker note.

macos.name: list_messages
macos.description: List the timeline of messages that have been COMPRESSED AWAY in this conversation, i.e. earlier messages that are no longer present in your current context because the conversation was summarized. Messages that are still in your context are NOT returned — do not use this tool to re-read what you already have.  Each entry gives: sequence number (#seq), message ID, role, timestamp, a short preview (<= 100 chars) and the names of any tools the message called. Deep-thinking (reasoning) content is never exposed.  Use it to: (1) discover the message ID of an earlier message and then read it with read_messages; (2) find earlier messages by keyword. The newest page of the queryable range is returned first; to page further back, call again with the returned cursor.

cursor.description: Page cursor: only return messages with sequence before this value. Omit it to get the newest page of the queryable range.

keyword.description: Optional keyword filter applied to the message plain text. Only messages in the queryable (compressed) range are searched.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages per page. Default: 30, Max: 50.

macos.name: read_messages
macos.description: Read the full text of earlier messages that have been COMPRESSED AWAY (they are no longer in your current context). Only messages before the compression summary can be read; anything still in your context is NOT returned.  Provide message_id (obtained from list_messages) and a relative window:   [-10, 0] = the anchor and the 10 messages before it;   [0, 10]  = the anchor and the 10 messages after it;   [-5, 5]  = 5 before and 5 after (default). If message_id (and seq) are omitted, the newest readable message is used as the anchor.  Limits: at most 21 messages per call, each message text <= 4000 chars, each tool-call detail <= 100 chars. Deep-thinking (reasoning) content is never returned. Do not call this repeatedly to dump the whole history.

message_id.description: Anchor message ID (from list_messages). Preferred over seq.

seq.description: Anchor message sequence number, used when message_id is not provided.

window.description: Relative window [start, end] around the anchor, with start <= 0 <= end. Examples: [-10,0] (10 before), [0,10] (10 after), [-5,5] (default).

linux.name: read_file
linux.description: Read a file's content. Returns content, line count, size, and hash10 (short fingerprint) (for edit_file conflict detection). Pass "paths" (array) to read multiple files in one call — avoids N round-trips for N files.

path.description: File path (relative to workspace or absolute). Use this for a single file.

paths.description: Array of file paths to read in one call. Use this to batch-read multiple files efficiently.

start_line.description: Starting line number (1-indexed). Use this to read a specific section of a large file. When set, returns at most max_lines lines starting from this line. Default: 1.

max_lines.description: Max lines to read. Default is 2000. When start_line is used, this limits how many lines are returned.

max_line_chars.description: Max characters per line. Default is 1600. Prevents token explosion from single very long lines (minified JS/CSS, long JSON/base64, etc.). Lines longer than this are truncated with a marker so the AI knows content is incomplete.

linux.name: write_file
linux.description: Write content to a file (full overwrite). Creates parent directories if they do not exist. ⚠️ Use edit_file for partial modifications instead of reading and re-writing entire files. Returns the hash10 (short fingerprint) of the written content (normalized to LF), which can be used as expected_hash for subsequent edit_file calls.

path.description: File path (relative to workspace or absolute).

linux.name: edit_file
linux.description: Replace exact text in a file. Requires expected_hash10 from read_file (conflict detection). Prefer for partial edits over write_file. Use the "edits" array to apply one or more edits in a single call — each edit is { old_string, new_string, replace_count }.

path.description: File path (relative to workspace or absolute).

edits.description: Array of edits to apply sequentially in one file. Each item: { old_string, new_string, replace_count }. All edits share the same expected_hash10 and are applied in order on the same content. Use this instead of multiple edit_file calls to avoid hash conflicts between edits.

old_string.description: The exact existing text to replace. Include enough surrounding context for a unique match.

new_string.description: The new text to insert in place of old_string.

replace_count.description: How many occurrences of old_string to replace. Default: 1. Set to 0 to replace all.

expected_hash.description: The hash10 value of the current file content, obtained from read_file output. Used for conflict detection to ensure no one modified the file since you read it.

linux.name: delete_file
linux.description: Delete one or more files/directories. Accepts either "path" (single string) or "paths" (array of strings). Deleted items are moved to trash/recycle bin.

path.description: Path to the file or directory to delete. Use this for a single item. (Deprecated in favor of "paths".)

paths.description: Array of paths to delete. Use this to delete multiple files/directories in one call.

items.description: Path to the file or directory to delete.

linux.name: copy_move_file
linux.description: Copy or move a file or directory. By default moves (renames) the source to destination. Set mode="copy" to copy instead. Note: copy mode only supports files, not directories; use move mode for directories.

source.description: Source file or directory path (relative to workspace or absolute).

destination.description: Destination file or directory path (relative to workspace or absolute).

mode.description: Operation mode: "move" (default) to move/rename, "copy" to copy.

linux.name: list_files
linux.description: List files and directories in a given path. Shows relative paths from the given root.

path.description: Directory path. Default: workspace root.

recursive.description: Whether to list recursively. Default: false

linux.name: file_info
linux.description: Get metadata about a file or directory.

path.description: Path to the file or directory.

linux.name: mkdir
linux.description: Create a directory (or directories). Pass "paths" (array) to create multiple directories in one call. By default creates parent directories if they do not exist (recursive=true). If a directory already exists, it is treated as success (idempotent).

path.description: Directory path to create (relative to workspace or absolute). Use this for a single directory.

paths.description: Array of directory paths to create in one call. Use this to batch-create multiple directories.

recursive.description: Whether to create parent directories if they do not exist. Default: true.

linux.name: search_files_by_name
linux.description: Search for files by filename. Supports plain text (case-insensitive substring match), regex matching (use_regex=true), or glob patterns (glob=true, e.g. "**/*.ts", "*.json", "src/**/*.css"). Returns a list of matching file paths.

path.description: Root directory to search in (e.g. "./src").

query.description: Filename pattern. Plain text (case-insensitive) by default, regex if use_regex=true, glob pattern if glob=true (e.g. "**/*.ts", "*.json", "src/**/*.css").

use_regex.description: Whether query is a regex pattern. Default: false.

glob.description: Whether query is a glob pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "*.json"). When true, overrides use_regex — converts glob to regex automatically. Default: false.

linux.name: search_text_in_files
linux.description: Search for text content inside files recursively. **Supports regex patterns.** Returns file path, line number, and the matching line content. Automatically skips binary files and respects .gitignore. Use this to find function definitions, variable usages, error messages, TODO comments, etc.

path.description: Root directory to search in (e.g. "./src").

query.description: Text or regex pattern to search for in file contents. Supports full regex syntax (e.g. "function\s+\w+" for function definitions, "TODO|FIXME" for TODOs).

linux.name: execute_command
linux.description: Execute an arbitrary shell command. The current terminal is sh (Linux/POSIX). Use this tool only when no dedicated tool exists (git, npm, builds, etc.). Prefer the dedicated tools (read_file, edit_file, write_file, search_*, ...) for file/text operations. The first line of the result is a "terminal environment" notice reporting the sandbox mode — "write isolation" (writes are allowed only inside the workspace/whitelisted writable roots; writes outside are rejected), "read-only" (no writes), or "no sandbox" (full permissions). An exit code >= 2 means the command failed.

command.description: The shell command to execute (sh/POSIX syntax), e.g. "ls -la", "git status", "node --version". Supports &&/|| chaining, pipelines and redirection.

tips.description: A brief explanation of what this command does and why it is being run (use the user's language). It is shown in the UI to help the user understand the purpose of the command.

sandbox.description: Omit by default (inherits the sandbox mode from settings). Passing "off" **requests** execution without the sandbox, and should only be used for cases that are bound to fail under the sandbox: the command's child process needs to spawn a grandchild process with piped stdio (vitest / vite / jest / ts-node / node-gyp / child_process.exec*, etc.), and the sandbox's restricted token makes that spawn fail immediately with EPERM (the log looks like "spawn EPERM"). This request goes through the "sandbox bypass" permission (a confirmation dialog by default; it can be set to allow or deny); in read-only sandbox mode it is rejected outright.

confirm.description: Passing "terminal" means "confirm in the terminal before executing": the command is shown as a single **editable** line, and actually runs only after the user edits it if needed and presses Enter; Esc cancels. Suited to commands the user must sign off on and may rewrite (e.g. commands that need login or input such as npm login / gh auth login). Execution still goes through the same sandbox path (a command written by the user is not exempt from checks); supported only on the Windows desktop, and falls back to the approval dialog when unavailable.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds. The process is killed after this period. Default: 30.

linux.name: execute_script
linux.description: Create a script file (file_path + file_content), then execute it with a shell command, and by default delete the script file right after execution (end_del_file=true). Use this instead of execute_command when the code to run is long/multi-line and awkward to inline. The file is written through the same sandbox check as write_file; the command goes through the same approval flow as execute_command. The first line of the result is a "terminal environment" notice; an exit code >= 2 means the command failed.

file_path.description: Path of the script file (relative to the workspace, or absolute), e.g. "temp/run.js". A sandbox check runs before writing.

file_content.description: Content of the script file (full overwrite). Missing parent directories are created automatically.

command.description: The command used to run the script file (sh/POSIX syntax), e.g. "node script.js", "python task.py", "sh run.sh". Reference the script file given by file_path; supports &&/|| chaining, pipelines and redirection.

tips.description: A brief explanation of what this command does and why it is being run (use the user's language). It is shown in the UI to help the user understand the purpose of the command.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds. The process is killed after this period. Default: 30.

sandbox.description: Omit by default (inherits the sandbox mode from settings). Passing "off" **requests** execution of the script without the sandbox, and should only be used for cases that are bound to fail under the sandbox (e.g. a child process inside the script needs to spawn a grandchild process with piped stdio). This request is decided by the "sandbox bypass · script execution" permission (a confirmation dialog by default); in read-only sandbox mode it is rejected outright.

end_del_file.description: Whether to delete the script file immediately after execution (including on failure/timeout). Default: true. Set to false to keep the script for troubleshooting.
